statement_summary: Security and Compliance Coordinator designated in writing
Annual risk assessment with SP 800-30; every risk owned and treated
Risk acceptance authority; SP 800-171 gaps never accepted
CUI only on SSP-listed CUI Assets; cloud only if FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent
Service providers: responsibility matrix, named MFA accounts, 24-hour incident notice, U.S.-person technicians
SSP kept current; no SPRS score or affirmation without evidence
Annual assessment against SP 800-171A; monthly POA&M review
Records kept 6 years; audit logs 1 year
Sanctions; good-faith reporting protected
Annual policy review; written, time-limited exceptions
Unique accounts everywhere CUI is reachable; no shared accounts or mailboxes
Least privilege; written approval; ITAR folders limited; no local admin for users
MFA for the CUI suite, every CUI computer, and every administrator login including the MSP's
Offboarding checklist on or before the last day
Monthly account check against the staff list; quarterly review by the President
Remote administration only through the RMM with MFA and logging; monthly session review
Phones only through the suite app with app protection, or blocked
Enclave computers wired; Wi-Fi key rotated yearly and at departures
10-minute screen lock on every computer
Visitor log, escort, foreign-person check, service engineer supervision, key register
Prime A portal is the only approved external system for CUI
One inventory with CMMC asset categories, updated within 30 days of change
Enclave network segment, deny by default
Monthly log review with the MSP; alerts for mass download, forwarding rules, foreign sign-ins
Work use only; no CUI outside approved systems; lock screens; no password sharing
Annual awareness training including CUI, phishing, insider threat, export control; role-based training
Report suspected incidents at once
Home work rules for company laptops
Signed acknowledgment at hire and yearly
Report suspected incidents immediately, by phone if email may be affected
Runbook, printed contacts, and DIBNet field list kept ready
DoD report through DIBNet within 72 hours; two medium assurance certificates kept current
Incident report number to the prime as soon as practicable
Review for compromise; preserve images and logs 90 days; no reimage before imaging
Quarantine malware for DC3; DoD requests through the President
Extortion approvals and OFAC check; export control disclosure decision; personal information notices
Lessons learned within 14 days; updates to risk register, POA&M, SSP, runbook
Annual tabletop with the MSP including a DIBNet login check
Classes (CUI, FCI, Internal, Public) and how to recognize CUI
CUI stored only in the CUI suite and CUI Assets; sent only through the suite or Prime A portal; ERP holds drawing numbers only
Customer markings kept; derived documents marked CUI
Approved AI tools only (none for CUI on 2026-09-01); public chatbots never; AI output never the source for dimensions or programs
Paper CUI printed on the shop printer only, returned to the locked cabinet each shift
Two company-owned encrypted USB drives only; logged, scanned, wiped; others destroyed
Cross-cut shredding; MSP wipe certificates before disposal or repair
Outside processors get process sheets, or flowed-down clauses and an SPRS check
ITAR technical data only for U.S. persons; Empowered Official decides access questions
FIPS-validated full-disk encryption on every computer and drive holding CUI
Backups only inside a FedRAMP Moderate-or-higher boundary; restore test twice a year
